chapter: Benny Meroff and Chicago's jazz scene
title: The theaters are sold and Meroff moves to the Oriental
summary: After the 1929 Crash the Marks brothers sell the theaters and Meroff's band is transferred to the Oriental.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: Yeah - much easier to read. Yeah. Well, of course, that's only the beginning of this thing -- I just made so much money and had so much fun that I just thought that that would go on forever and ever.
Well, it did go on for a long time for musicians at that time.
Yeah well, when this tape runs out [Pause] Well, anyway, it was about
... this time that Meroff was approached about the fact that the Marks brothers were selling the two theaters, after we'd been there a couple years.
The Marks brothers being the guys who owned this chain, not Groucho.

Who owned the Balvin & Katz chain. And we all got nervous as hell, including Meroff. Of course, we had the best band in town. There was no doubt that we had the best show band in the whole city. And whenever there was something special to do they picked on the Meroff band. So we all got very nervous until we one day found out that the theater--the two Marks brothers theaters--were sold. And we were transferred to the Oriental. And of course that is the epitome in Chicago, to be at the Oriental or Chicago theater. We were scheduled to go to the Oriental. But we were going to stay at the Oriental. No more moving around, you see.
This was a year or so after you joined the band?
So it was probably toward the end of 1929. That's the period you're talking about.
Yeah, the Crash had already taken place.
Yes. I was still at the Marlborough when the Crash took place.
